'''Virginia "Ginger" Patricia McShane Warfield''' is an American mathematician and mathematical educator. She received the [[Louise Hay Award]] from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kelley |first1=Peter |title=Teacher's teacher: 'Ginger' Warfield wins national math education award |url=http://www.washington.edu/news/2007/01/11/teachers-teacher-ginger-warfield-wins-national-math-education-award/ |website=UW News |access-date=7 April 2019}}</ref>

==Education==

Warfield's father was mathematician [[Edward J. McShane]].<ref name="NYT">[https://www.nytimes.com/1989/06/06/obituaries/edward-mcshane-85-mathematician-dies.html New York Times:Edward McShane, 85, Mathematician, Dies; June 06, 1989]</ref> She received her Ph.D. in mathematics from Brown University in 1971. Her doctoral advisor was [[Wendell Fleming]] and the title of her dissertation was ''A Stochastic Maximum Principle''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Virginia P. Warfield |url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=4406 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=7 April 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
While making contributions to the field of stochastic analysis after her Ph.D., Warfield became more and more engrossed by the problems of mathematics education. She worked with Project SEED, a highly regarded mathematics program whose goal was to promote sense-making mathematical activities for fourth through sixth graders. She addressed issues of teacher preparation and enhancement. She collaborated with the French mathematician Guy
Brousseau, a pioneer in the “didactics of mathematics,” the scientific study of issues in mathematics teaching and learning.<ref name="hayaward">{{cite web |title=Virginia McShane Warfield Honored With Hay Award |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gAHiClbSyN8Ma6dKAmrWXSwPuWrFIdXR/view?usp=sharing |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |access-date=7 April 2019}}</ref> She has been an active member of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM). She has chaired the Education Committee, has served as Education Column Editor for the AWM Newsletter, and was elected as a Member-at-large to the Executive Committee. She has been a member of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]’s committees on Professional Development and Mathematical Education of Teachers.<ref name="hayaward" />

==Books==
Warfield is the author of the book ''Invitation to Didactique'' (self-published, 2007, and Springer Briefs in Education, 2014)<ref>{{cite web|title=Review of ''Invitation to Didactique''|work=MAA Reviews|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|first=Stephen|last=Lancaster|date=January 16, 2008|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/invitation-to-didactique-0}}</ref> and the co-author of ''Teaching Fractions through Situations: A Fundamental Experiment'' (with Guy Brousseau and Nadine Brousseau, Springer 2013).<ref>{{cite web|title=Review of ''Teaching Fractions through Situations''|first=Annie|last=Selden|author-link=Annie Selden|work=MAA Reviews|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|date=February 22, 2014|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/teaching-fractions-through-situations-a-fundamental-experiment}}</ref>
